about: This is the reserve bottling from the Goldschmidt family, New Zealanders who settled in Healdsburg in 1990. Nick Goldschmidt was chief winemaker at Simi in the 1990s and later ran winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates before building his own label, which he keeps to single vineyards and single varieties. He still consults in New Zealand, Chile and Argentina after each Sonoma harvest, and three of his daughters, Chelsea, Hilary and Katherine, now make wine under his guidance.

The fruit comes from the Singing Tree site, a hillside near Sebastopol in the cool, fog-cooled western Russian River Valley, farmed as part of the Dutton Ranch family of vineyards. The vines date from 1987 and grow in sandy Gold Ridge loam, a soil prized for Chardonnay because it drains freely and keeps yields modest. For the reserve, Nick selects a smaller portion of the crop and gives it more time and more barrel influence than the regular Singing Tree.

Tasting notes for the 2021 point to baked pear, honey, hazelnut and a touch of melon, with citrus and a little vanilla on a bright palate and a mineral, wet-stone finish. Look too for lily of the valley, peach blossom and toasted almond, a richer and rounder counterpart to the by-the-glass Singing Tree. James Suckling scored it 91 points.
